title: Boosting Bot Detection via Heterophily-Aware Representation Learning and Prototype-Guided Cluster Discovery

problem.claim: Social media bot detection is needed to maintain the security and trustworthiness of social networks.

gap.claim: Existing graph-based bot detection methods rely heavily on labels, generalize poorly across communities, predominantly assume homophily, and fail to capture global graph patterns.

contributions.claim: BotHP is a generative graph self-supervised learning framework using heterophily-aware representation learning and prototype-guided cluster discovery.
BotHP uses a dual-encoder architecture with graph-aware and graph-agnostic encoders to model node commonality and uniqueness.
BotHP uses prototype-guided cluster discovery to model latent global consistency in bot clusters and identify spatially dispersed but semantically aligned bot collectives.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two real-world bot detection benchmarks reportedly show that BotHP consistently boosts graph-based bot detectors.
The authors report improved detection performance, reduced label reliance, and enhanced generalization capability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Bot detection is important for social network security and trustworthiness.
Current graph-based approaches face label dependence, poor cross-community generalization, homophily assumptions, and limited global-pattern modeling.
BotHP addresses these limitations with heterophily-aware representation learning and prototype-guided cluster discovery.
The dual encoders jointly model homophily and heterophily, while cluster discovery models global bot-cluster consistency.
The authors report gains across two real-world benchmarks in detection performance, label reliance, and generalization.
